findings.summary: `*` and `+` empty bullets now interrupt paragraphs, a deviation beyond the documented `-` fix
findings.evidence:
`isEmptyBulletLine` accepts `-`, `*` and `+` (line 39), and `wrappedList` returns true for any of them when silently probed from a paragraph. But only `-` has the lheading/setext ambiguity the change exists to fix. Consequence: `foo\n*` previously rendered as paragraph text (`foo
*` under `breaks: true`) and now renders `

foo

`, silently swallowing a literal asterisk line. Same for `foo\n+`. Neither the design doc (which speaks only of `-`) nor any test covers this.

findings.summary: Local `asciiTrim` diverges from upstream lheading's `String.prototype.trim()`
findings.evidence: The forked rule builds heading content with `asciiTrim(state.getLines(...))` (line 134-136) and the comment claims markdown-it uses an `asciiTrim` here. markdown-it 14's `rules_block/lheading.mjs` uses plain `.trim()`, which also strips non-ASCII whitespace (NBSP U+00A0, U+2028, U+FEFF). With this reimplementation a setext heading whose text ends in a NBSP keeps that character in the rendered `<h2>`, a silent divergence from stock rendering. node_modules was not installed in the worktree so the upstream source could not be confirmed here.

findings.summary: `getRuleFn` reads a private markdown-it field and throws during module evaluation
findings.evidence: `ruler.__rules__.find(...)` plus `throw new Error(...)` (lines 211-213) runs from `listEmptyBulletPlugin` which is invoked at module scope in preview.ts:48 (`md.use(listEmptyBulletPlugin)`). If markdown-it ever renames/reshapes `__rules__` (it is private, not covered by semver), `ruler.__rules__` is `undefined` and `.find` throws a TypeError at import time, taking down the whole notes preview module rather than degrading to stock rendering. `md.block.ruler.getRules('paragraph')` filtered by name, or a try/catch fallback that skips the wrapper, would fail soft.

findings.summary: Silent shortcut omits upstream `list`'s 4-space indented-code guard
findings.evidence: `wrappedList` returns true whenever `silent && parentType === 'paragraph' && isEmptyBulletLine(...)`, but `isEmptyBulletLine` only checks `state.sCount[line] >= state.blkIndent` (line 32) — it never rejects `state.sCount[line] - state.blkIndent >= 4`, which upstream `list` treats as an indented code block. Today this is masked because both `paragraph` and the forked `lheading` `continue` past lines indented >3 before consulting terminator rules, so the branch is unreachable; but any other rule that probes `list` silently while `parentType === 'paragraph'` would get a spurious paragraph termination for an indented-code line. Worth mirroring upstream's indent check for safety.

findings.summary: Forked `lheading` will silently drift from upstream on markdown-it upgrades
findings.evidence: `lheadingRule` (lines 70-155) is a full copy of markdown-it 14.x's rule installed via `md.block.ruler.at('lheading', ...)`, so any upstream bug fix or CommonMark spec correction to `lheading` in a `^14` patch/minor bump is silently discarded — the copy keeps whatever markdown-it 14.1 did, with nothing in CI comparing the two. A wrapper that delegates to the original fn and only vetoes the lone-dash case (as is done for `list`) would not have this drift.

findings.summary: Falling through to terminator rules can hand the lone-dash line to `table` instead of the list
findings.evidence:
When `isLoneDash` is true the rule falls through to the paragraph terminator chain (lines 118-126). `table` is first in that chain, so for input `foo\n-\n---` the `-` line is consumed as a table header row (`---` being a valid one-column delimiter row) rather than by `list`: the result is a paragraph plus a ``, where before it was `

foo

`. The comment at lines 102-104 assumes the list rule is the one that will pick the line up; it is not guaranteed.

findings.summary: Deviation is broader than the issue: ANY lone single-dash setext underline stops being a heading, including top-level `Heading\n-` outside any list. The issue (#517) and the task's acceptance criteria only describe the nested-empty-bullet case; the guard could have been scoped to lines inside/indented under a list. It is documented as deliberate in docs/design/notes/notes.md:293-299, so this is a scope/taste call rather than a hard violation, but it silently changes a valid CommonMark construct the issue never mentioned.
findings.evidence: const isLoneDash = marker === DASH && runLength === 1; — applied unconditionally in the replacement lheading rule, with no check that the line participates in a list context.

findings.summary: Approach fit: the `lheading` rule is forked wholesale (~60 lines copied from markdown-it 14.x `rules_block/lheading.mjs`, plus a re-implementation of markdown-it's private `asciiTrim`) for a one-line semantic change. The file already demonstrates the delegate-to-original pattern (`getRuleFn` + `wrappedList`); not using it for `lheading` duplicates upstream code that will silently drift on any markdown-it upgrade (no test pins the copy against upstream).

findings.summary: Depends on markdown-it's private `__rules__` registry to recover the stock `list` rule. This couples notes rendering to an undocumented internal shape; a markdown-it minor upgrade that renames/reshapes it turns into a runtime throw (or, worse, a silent behavior change) rather than a type error. A more contained approach (e.g. capturing the rule before replacement via a fresh MarkdownIt instance, or re-implementing only the interrupt guard) would avoid private-API reliance.

findings.summary: New undocumented plugin-ordering invariant: any plugin registered after `listEmptyBulletPlugin` that replaces `list`/`lheading` silently discards this fix, and any plugin added before it gets its `list` wrapper permanently baked in
findings.evidence: `getRuleFn` snapshots the `list` rule at install time and `md.block.ruler.at('lheading', ...)` overwrites whatever is registered. Today `md.use(taskLists)` (preview.ts:36), `md.use(katexPlugin)` (preview.ts:39) and `md.use(detailsPlugin)` (preview.ts:44) all run first and none replace `list`/`lheading`, so the current chain is fine — but the ordering requirement exists only implicitly. `packages/notes/src/view/details-plugin.ts:104-106` registers `details` with `alt: ['paragraph','reference','blockquote','list']`, showing plugins here do touch the same ruler surfaces. A comment at preview.ts:46-48 stating 'must stay last / after any plugin touching list or lheading' would preserve the invariant.

findings.summary: `Ruler.at('lheading', fn)` with no options resets the rule's `alt` chain; the code restores `alt` for `list` but not for `lheading`
findings.evidence: list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:197-199 explicitly restores `alt: ['paragraph','reference','blockquote']` for `list` with the comment that `Ruler.at` wipes the alt chain, but line 175 calls `md.block.ruler.at('lheading', lheadingRule)` with no options. In stock markdown-it 14 `parser_block` the `lheading` entry is registered without an alt list, so this is very likely a no-op — I could not verify against `node_modules` (dependencies are not installed in this worktree). If upstream ever gives `lheading` an alt chain, or if a plugin loaded earlier had set one, this silently drops it and `lheading` stops terminating paragraphs/blockquotes.

findings.summary: Hand-rolled trim regex backtracks quadratically (ReDoS) on attacker-controlled note content, replacing upstream's linear `.trim()`
findings.evidence: `ASCII_TRIM_RE = /^[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+|[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+$/g` (lines 19-20) is applied at line 134 to `state.getLines(startLine, nextLine, state.blkIndent, false)` — the full setext-heading paragraph body, i.e. untrusted note text. The first alternative is cheap (`^` without `m` only matches at index 0), but the second, `[ws]+$`, is unanchored at the start: `String.replace` with the `g` flag retries at every offset, and at each offset inside a whitespace run of length k it greedily consumes the rest of the run, fails `$` on the following non-whitespace char, and backtracks one char at a time — O(k) per offset, O(k^2) total. Attack: any workspace member with write access stores content like `x` + `' '.repeat(200000)` + `y\n===` (or the same run on a line above `---`). When a victim opens the note, `NotePreview.render()` (packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:165) calls `md.render()`, `lheading` matches (level set at line 108) and the trim at line 134 burns ~1e10 backtracking steps, hanging the victim's tab — and re-hanging on every subsequent re-render. Upstream markdown-it's `lheading` trims linearly here, so this quadratic path is introduced by the change. Fix: trim by index scan, or use non-global start-anchored matches, or `String.prototype.trim()`.

findings.summary: Reaching into markdown-it's private `__rules__` and throwing at import time makes the entire notes preview unavailable on dependency drift
findings.evidence: `getRuleFn` (lines 207-214) reads the undocumented private `ruler.__rules__` and does `throw new Error(...)` if the entry is missing. `listEmptyBulletPlugin` executes during module evaluation of `preview.ts` (`md.use(listEmptyBulletPlugin)`, preview.ts:48), and packages/notes/package.json pins `markdown-it: ^14.1.0` — a caret range — so a transparent minor/patch bump that renames or restructures that private field converts a rendering degradation into a hard import-time exception that takes out every consumer of `preview.ts` (imported by packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:20), not just setext handling. Availability-only, and contingent on future upstream change, hence low confidence; a non-throwing fallback that leaves stock behavior intact would be safer than failing the module import.

verdict.reason: The code is present as quoted (list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:105/107 has no blkIndent or list-parent condition, and wrappedList at :181-193 terminates any paragraph on an empty bullet), so the described top-level behavior change is real. However it is not a correctness defect: it exactly implements the documented intent. docs/design/notes/notes.md:293-299 states the deviation as "a **lone single `-`** (the empty-bullet shape) is never a setext underline, and an empty bullet is allowed to interrupt a paragraph" — unconditional, with "narrowly" defined by the following sentence as multi-dash `---` and `=` underlines being untouched, not as list-scoped. The plugin's own contract comments (:55-68, :157-172) say the same. There is no wrong condition relative to intent, no crash, no data loss, and no broken invariant; the source markdown is unchanged (preview-only rendering choice, notes.md:298-299). Objecting to the chosen CommonMark deviation is a spec/design-fit argument owned by another lens, not the Correctness lane, which judges implementation against intent — and here they agree.

verdict.reason:
The finding claims the `alt: ['paragraph','reference','blockquote']` restoration after `Ruler.at` is untested and that dropping it would leave the suite green. That is refuted by existing tests. The plugin's empty-bullet branch (list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:181-193) only triggers when `silent && state.parentType === 'paragraph'`, i.e. only when `list` is present in the `'paragraph'` terminator chain that the `alt` option restores at lines 197-199. markdown-it 14.x `Ruler.at` sets `alt = opt.alt || []`, so removing/emptying the option removes `list` from `getRules('paragraph')`. Three tests then fail: preview.test.ts:153-166 ('- 1
  -' expects a nested empty <li> and no <h2>; without the alt chain the lone dash is absorbed as lazy paragraph continuation and `expect(nested).toBeTruthy()` fails), preview.test.ts:168-173 ('- 1
  - ' expects `ul > li > ul > li`), and preview.test.ts:189-195 ('- 1
  - 2' expects nested text '2', which requires the nested list to interrupt the item's paragraph via the same alt chain). So the restoration is meaningfully exercised, and the tests are not "plain top-level lists" only. I did search beyond the reviewer's path — all NotePreview consumers (only preview.test.ts), every notes/frontend test file, e2e globs, and any other markdown-it renderer — and confirmed no blockquote/link-reference fixture exists; but that residual gap is only the case where one alt member is deleted while 'paragraph' survives, which is breadth-of-coverage (minor) rather than a behavior change with no meaningful test, and the rubric excludes "add more tests" from blocking.

samples.summary: Hand-rolled trim regex backtracks quadratically (ReDoS) on attacker-controlled note content, replacing upstream's linear `.trim()`
samples.evidence: `ASCII_TRIM_RE = /^[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+|[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+$/g` (lines 19-20) is applied at line 134 to `state.getLines(startLine, nextLine, state.blkIndent, false)` — the full setext-heading paragraph body, i.e. untrusted note text. The first alternative is cheap (`^` without `m` only matches at index 0), but the second, `[ws]+$`, is unanchored at the start: `String.replace` with the `g` flag retries at every offset, and at each offset inside a whitespace run of length k it greedily consumes the rest of the run, fails `$` on the following non-whitespace char, and backtracks one char at a time — O(k) per offset, O(k^2) total. Attack: any workspace member with write access stores content like `x` + `' '.repeat(200000)` + `y\n===` (or the same run on a line above `---`). When a victim opens the note, `NotePreview.render()` (packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:165) calls `md.render()`, `lheading` matches (level set at line 108) and the trim at line 134 burns ~1e10 backtracking steps, hanging the victim's tab — and re-hanging on every subsequent re-render. Upstream markdown-it's `lheading` trims linearly here, so this quadratic path is introduced by the change. Fix: trim by index scan, or use non-global start-anchored matches, or `String.prototype.trim()`.

verdict.reason: Every element of the claim checks out against the repository. The regex at list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:19-20 is verbatim as quoted, including the `g` flag, and is applied via `asciiTrim` (line 22) at line 134 to `state.getLines(startLine, nextLine, state.blkIndent, false)` — the raw setext-heading paragraph body. The second alternative `[\x09\x0a\x0b\x0c\x0d\x20]+$` is unanchored at the start, so `String.replace` with `g` retries at every offset; inside a whitespace run of length k followed by a non-whitespace char it greedily consumes the run and backtracks one char at a time re-failing `$`, giving O(k) per offset and O(k^2) overall. This is the established trailing-whitespace trim ReDoS class (CWE-1333, cf. the trim-newlines `/[\r\n]+$/` advisory), not a speculative pattern. Reachability with attacker-controlled input is confirmed: preview.ts:48 registers the plugin (which replaces the `lheading` rule at line 175) on the shared `md` instance, and preview.ts:164-165 calls `md.render(markdown)` on note content; the file's own SECURITY comment at preview.ts:120-126 establishes that note content is authored by other workspace members and rendered in a victim's session. The `isLoneDash` guard at line 105 only excludes a single `-`, so `===` or `---` underlines still set `level` at line 108 and reach the trim. `getLines` only strips leading block indent, so an interior run such as `x` + many spaces + `y` survives into `content` intact. I found no length or whitespace-run bound anywhere before render, and `asciiTrim` has no other call sites that could interpose a check. Untrusted-input DoS is not in this lens's excluded list, so I cannot rule it out of lane; impact is limited to hanging the victim's tab (no data or auth compromise), which matches the `major` severity given. No refutation ground applies.
